<p class="page-deck">An ongoing paper mapping where urban climate evidence is produced and examining the conditions under which documented findings may be relevant to other cities.</p>

## The problem

Urban climate research is unevenly distributed, while the visibility or apparent similarity of a city does not establish that its evidence applies elsewhere.

## What this work asks

Where is urban climate evidence produced, and under which contextual conditions may documented findings be informative to other cities?

- How is urban climate evidence distributed across cities and regions?
- Under what conditions may evidence be relevant to other cities?

## How the work investigates it

The ongoing paper maps the geography of documented urban climate evidence and examines contextual conditions that may shape relevance across places.

## What better understanding could make possible

The work could help comparative researchers distinguish the visibility of a precedent from the conditions under which another city might plausibly learn from it.

## Evidence status and boundaries

**Evidence status.** Ongoing research grounded in a verified preprint; ongoing findings are not inferred here.

**Claim boundaries.** Geographic proximity, similarity or evidence volume alone does not establish applicability or transferability.
